note: The reviewed Plane surface. `tools` is what ships, with the reason it ships; `excluded` is what stays out, with the rule that keeps it out; `pending` is what has not been reviewed yet. Plane publishes no spec, so the pin in scripts/plane/inventory.json is what these decisions are made against and scripts/plane/endpoints.mjs is what they are turned into. Regenerate with npm run gen:plane-routes after a change here.

p1.note: Reads: one GET each, no body, so nothing here can change a workspace.

p2.note: Writes: one request each, every one behind a confirm gate; the destructive ones are argued in destructive.ts as well.

tools.reason: The customer directory: the way in to customers, their requests and their linked work items.
One customer by id, for the detail a listing narrows to.
The work items filed against a customer, which is how customer work is actually tracked.
The workspace's customer property definitions, needed to read any customer's values.
One property definition, including the options a value has to come from.
The requests a customer has raised: the queue that customer work starts from.
One request, with the link and description a listing leaves out.
One cycle, whose dates and ownership the project's schedule is read from.
What is planned into a cycle: the reading that answers whether a sprint is on track.
The workspace's initiatives, the level above projects that outcomes are reported at.
One initiative, with the state and lead a listing does not carry.
A project's intake queue: work proposed from outside the project, before it is accepted.
One intake item, which a triage decision is made on.
A project's labels, the vocabulary its work items are filtered by.
One label by id, for the parent and colour a listing flattens.
Who the stored token belongs to: the identity a write is attributed to.
The workspace's members, which is how a UUID in any other response is turned into a person.
A project's members, for the people a work item can be assigned to.
The role catalogue, whose slugs are the values the member listing filters on.
A project's milestones with their target dates: the readings a delivery date is checked against.
One milestone by id, for the fields a listing truncates.
What is filed under a milestone: the progress behind its target date.
One module, whose status and members make it a workstream rather than a label.
What a module contains, for reading scope without loading the whole project.
The pages attached to one work item: the notes that travel with it.
The project directory. It reads Plane's compact listing, which is what the vendor's own tools browse with.
One project, for the identifier and defaults every other call is scoped by.
Total logged time per project, which no work-item listing aggregates.
Which features a project has switched on, the state `project.update-features` would change.
A project's estimate: the scale that gives its points meaning.
The points of that estimate, which is what a work item's point value refers to.
The workspace's releases, the container work items are shipped in.
One release, with the dates and lead a listing leaves out.
The release notes: read before editing them, because Plane creates the changelog empty on first read.
What a release carries, which is the question a release page exists to answer.
The release tags a release can be pinned to: version identifiers, not git refs.
One tag by id, for the commit hash a listing does not show.
A project's workflow states, which every work item's `state` argument has to name.
tools.flowNote: The vendor's action forks on project_id: with it the project's states, without it the workspace catalogue. This tool ships the project branch and refuses a call without project_id, so one tool is still one endpoint.

tools.reason: One state by id: its group tells a reader whether a work item counts as started or done.
tools.flowNote: Project-scoped, like state.list: a workspace state id is not accepted, and the refusal names project_id.

tools.reason: Time logged against one work item, the records the project summary is computed from.
One work item by UUID, with the optional expansions a search result does not carry.
One work item by its human key (PROJECT-123), which is how people refer to work in a conversation.
Workspace-wide work-item search: the only read that crosses projects.
A work item's history, which says who changed what and when.
The attachments on a work item, for the evidence a description only points at.
A work item's comments, which is where the decisions about it actually live.
One comment by id, so a reply can quote it without fetching the whole thread.
The links hanging off a work item: pull requests, documents, dashboards.
One link by id, for the metadata Plane stores beside the URL.
One option of a project property, which is the value set a work item can be given.
tools.flowNote: The vendor forks on project_id between a project's property options and the workspace catalogue. This ships the project branch and refuses a call without project_id.

tools.reason: One custom property value on one work item: the fields Plane does not model natively.
A project's work-item types, which are the values `type_id` accepts and the scope a property is read at.
tools.flowNote: The vendor forks on project_id between a project's types and the workspace catalogue. This ships the project branch and refuses a call without project_id.

tools.reason: One work-item type, whose properties decide what a work item of that type carries.
tools.flowNote: Project-scoped, like workitem_type.list; the workspace type catalogue is not exposed.

tools.reason: Which workspace features are on, so a caller can tell a missing feature from a missing permission.
The templates a project creates pages or work items from: the shapes a team has agreed on.
tools.flowNote: Two forks, both narrowed: project_id selects one project's templates rather than the workspace catalogue, and `kind` selects page or work-item templates. A `kind` of `project` exists only at workspace scope, so it is refused.
tools.variantNote: `kind` selects the collection: workitem templates or page templates.

tools.reason: The wiki collections in the workspace, which is how pages are grouped and shared.
One collection by id, with the access level its pages inherit.
The pages in a collection, including the nesting a search result flattens.
Search inside one collection, which the page listing cannot express.
Who a collection is shared with, and at what access level.
